s1.syndrome_frame: inflammatory arthritis and skin lesions with systemic symptoms
key_facts: man in his 50s
dermal papules on trunk and extremities
preference for extensor surfaces of arms and legs
no lymphadenopathy
relief of symptoms with daily oral prednisone
flare of symptoms with taper below 10 mg
previous treatments included hydroxychloroquine and adalimumab without improvement
mild restrictive disease on pulmonary function tests
nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate on skin biopsy
atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes on skin biopsy
low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal on immunostaining
clonal rearrangements identified in skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow sample

raw.syndrome_frame: inflammatory arthritis and skin lesions with systemic symptoms
key_facts: man in his 50s
dermal papules on trunk and extremities
preference for extensor surfaces of arms and legs
no lymphadenopathy
relief of symptoms with daily oral prednisone
flare of symptoms with taper below 10 mg
previous treatments included hydroxychloroquine and adalimumab without improvement

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: presence of atypical lymphocytes and clonal rearrangements in skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow sample

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: dermal papules and inflammatory arthritis, with relief of symptoms with daily oral prednisone

shortlist.label: Amyopathic dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions and mild restrictive disease on pulmonary function tests, without muscle involvement

shortlist.label: Erythema elevatum diutinum
shortlist.why_kept: presence of pink-purple dermal papules, particularly on extensor surfaces

shortlist.label: Granuloma annulare
shortlist.why_kept: nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate on skin biopsy

shortlist.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
shortlist.why_kept: presence of atypical lymphocytes and histiocytes on skin biopsy

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: mild restrictive disease on pulmonary function tests and granulomatous inflammation

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: inflammatory arthritis, skin lesions, and systemic symptoms, although less likely given the specific biopsy findings

raw.rationale: The presence of clonal rearrangements in skin biopsy specimens and bone marrow, along with atypical lymphocytes and a nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, supports the diagnosis of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. The patient's response to prednisone and the lack of improvement with other treatments also align with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The absence of muscle weakness and the presence of atypical lymphocytes with a low CD4 signal and robust CD8 signal do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Amyopathic dermatomyositis
rejected.why: The patient's skin findings and lack of muscle involvement do not fully align with this diagnosis, and the presence of atypical lymphocytes suggests a different condition.

rejected.label: Erythema elevatum diutinum
rejected.why: The patient's skin lesions and systemic symptoms do not match the typical presentation of erythema elevatum diutinum, which is characterized by tender, red-brown plaques on the extensor surfaces.

rejected.label: Granuloma annulare
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy findings and systemic symptoms do not support a diagnosis of granuloma annulare, which typically presents with localized, annular plaques.

rejected.label: Necrobiotic xanthogranuloma
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy findings and lack of characteristic yellowish plaques do not support a diagnosis of necrobiotic xanthogranuloma.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy findings and lack of granulomas do not support a diagnosis of sarcoidosis, which typically presents with non-caseating granulomas in affected tissues.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy findings and lack of characteristic systemic symptoms, such as renal involvement or positive antinuclear antibodies, do not support a diagnosis of lupus erythematosus.
